answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and posts a quote on the wharf board each epoch, in its karst cell, and the board enforces a nadir floor of 30 credits per job. A below-floor quote is rejected and its bond burned. The identity signs its quote with its key, so one quote cannot serve two identities, and auditors recompute each cell from the board. A shared key or cell collapses two identities to one entry and burns both bonds, so a floor-dodging ring renting quotes exposes itself. Creating 1,000 fakes locks 80,000 credits plus 15 each, 95,000 total, while one honest identity pays 95 once.
